 Presented on : 27-03-2019
 Registered on : 28-03-2019

 Duration : 5 years, 3 months, 28 days
 In The Court Of The Judicial Magistrate First
 Class (Traffic Court-Vi), Bengaluru City. 
 Dated This 24Th Day Of July 2024. 
 Present : Smt .AKHILA H.K. B.A., Ll.B.,
 Jmfc (Traffic Court-Vi),
 Bengaluru. 
 Cc No.2304/2019
Complainant: State by Hsr Layout Traffic P.S
 Bengaluru.
 (State by : Learned App) 
 V/s ACCUSED: Maria Robhinath  S/o R.S. Pandian  Aged about 34 years,
 No.99, Ground Floor, 4th Cross,
 CSB Layout, Kasavanahalli,
 Bengaluru - 560 035.
 (Represented by Sri.V.R., Adv.,)
 CC No.2304/2019  2  JUDGMENT The Police Inspector of HSR Layout Traffic Police Station has filed charge sheet against the accused for the offence punishable U/Sec.279 and 338 of IPC, Sec.134(A & B) R/w Sec.187 & Sec.146 R/w 196 of IMV Act.
2. The brief facts of the prosecution case are as under: -

1 That on 14.10.2018 at 1.00 a.m. accused being the rider of Bullet motor cycle bearing registration No.TN-58- P-6924 rode the same within the jurisdiction of H.S.R.
Layout Traffic Police station on Sarjapura main road from Bellanduru police station towards Ibbaluru junction at a high speed in a rash and negligent manner so as to endanger human life and opposite to Trinity Acres & Woods Apartment hit to C.W.2 when he proceeding in the edge of the road after crossing the Sarjapura main road from Drops wine towards Trinity Acres & Wood apartment. As a result C.W.2 sustained grievous injuries on his head. Further, after the accident accused has failed to provide medical assistance to the injured and also failed to inform the same to the nearest police CC No.2304/2019 station and at the time of accident offending vehicle did not have valid insurance. As such the accused has committed an offence punishable U/Sec.279 and 338 of IPC, Sec.134(A & B) R/w Sec.187 & Sec.146 R/w 196 of IMV Act. 
3. Cognizance was taken by perusing the prosecution papers and materials, the accused on receipt of summons appeared before the court and got himself enlarged on bail. On the said date the prosecution papers were furnished to the accused as per Sec.207 of Cr.P.C. and substance of accusation in the form of plea was read over and explained to him, accused pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried. 
4. During the course of trial the prosecution has examined PWs.1 to 5 and got marked Ex.P.1 to 11. 
The statement of accused as per Sec.313 of Cr.P.C. was recorded the accused had no explanation and he denied the incriminating circumstances appearing against him. 
5. Heard both sides. 
CC No.2304/2019 6. The point that arises for my determination is as under:
1. Whether the prosecution proves beyond all reasonable doubt that, on 14.10.2018 at 1.00 a.m. accused being the rider of Bullet motor cycle bearing registration No.TN-58-P-6924 rode the same within the jurisdiction of H.S.R. Layout Traffic Police station on Sarjapura main road from Bellanduru police station towards Ibbaluru junction in a rash and negligent manner so as to endanger human life,
thereby committed an offence punishable under Sec.279 of IPC Act? 
2. Whether the prosecution proves beyond all reasonable doubt that, on the same date, time and place accused drove his vehicle in a rash CC No.2304/2019 and negligent manner and opposite to Trinity Acres & Woods Apartment hit to C.W.2 when he proceeding in the edge of the road after crossing the Sarjapura main road from Drops wine towards Trinity Acres & Wood apartment. As a result C.W.2 sustained grievous injuries on his head, thereby accused committed an offence punishable U/Sec.338 of IPC ? 
H S Rlay Out Tr Ps vs Maria Robhinath on 24 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/95040995/
2 3. Whether the prosecution proves beyond reasonable doubt that, after the accident accused has failed to provide medical assistance to the accused and also failed to inform the same to the nearest police station, thereby accused committed an offence punishable under Sec.134 (A & B) R/w Sec.187 of IMV Act?
CC No.2304/2019 4. Whether the prosecution proves beyond reasonable doubt that, at the time of accident offending vehicle did not have valid insurance thereby accused committed an offence punishable U/Sec.146 R/w Sec.196 of IMV Act?
5. What Order? 
7. My answer to the above points are as under:
Point No.1 : In the negative;
Point No.2 : In the negative;
Point No.3 : In the negative;
Point No.4 : In the affirmative; Point No.5 : As per final order for the following;
REASONS 8. Point No.1 to 4: For the sake of convenience and to avoid repetition of facts, these points are taken up for common discussions to have brevity.
CC No.2304/2019 9. The prosecution case against the accused is that on 14.10.2018 at 1.00 a.m. accused being the rider of Bullet motor cycle bearing registration No.TN-58-P- 6924 rode the same within the jurisdiction of H.S.R. Layout Traffic Police station on Sarjapura main road from Bellanduru police station towards Ibbaluru junction at a high speed in a rash and negligent manner so as to endanger human life and opposite to Trinity Acres & Woods Apartment hit to C.W.2 when he proceeding in the edge of the road after crossing the Sarjapura main road from Drops wine towards Trinity Acres & Wood apartment. As a result C.W.2 sustained grievous injuries on his head. Further, after the accident accused has failed to provide medical assistance to the injures and also failed to inform the same to the nearest police station and at the time of accident offending vehicle did not have valid insurance. 
10. In order to bring home the charge against the accused the prosecution has examined 5 witnesses as PWs.1 to 5 and got marked Ex.P.1 to 11. Ex.P.1 is the spot mahazar, Ex.P.2 is the 4 photos, Ex.P.3 is the CC No.2304/2019 complaint, Ex.P.4 is the FIR, Ex.P.5 is the rough sketch, Ex.P.6 & 7 are the H S Rlay Out Tr Ps vs Maria Robhinath on 24 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/95040995/
3 notice and reply U/Sec.133 of IMV Act, Ex.P.8 is the police notice, Ex.P.9 is the wound certificate,
Ex.P.10 is the IMV report and Ex.P.11 is the indemnity bond. 
11. Before adverting to the appreciation of evidence it is proper to state in brief the evidence deposed by the prosecution witnesses. 
12. C.W.3 examined as P.W.1 is the eye witness and mahazar witness. He deposed that, on 14.10.2018 at 12.30 to 1.00 a.m. he, C.W.1, 2, 4 and 5 after having food at Koramangala they have proceeded towards Trinity in a cab and opposite to Trinity there is one wine shop and there they get down from the cab and they were trying to cross the road and C.W.2 was crossing the road and remaining 4 of them were standing on the divider meanwhile one two wheeler bearing No.TN-58-P-6924 came in rash and negligent manner and hit to C.W.2, as a result C.W.2 sustained injuries on his head, leg and CC No.2304/2019 hand and he was unconscious and shifted to Columbia Asia hospital. With this regard C.W.1 has lodged a complaint/Ex.P.1. On the same day at 10.00 a.m police conducted spot mahazar/Ex.P.1 in his and C.W.1's presence and obtained his signature on it. Further he deposed that, accident has occurred due to the fault of the rider of the offending vehicle. 
13. In his cross examination he has admitted that, they saw the bike from a distance of 8-10 feet and he has also admitted that himself and C.W.2, 4 and 5 did not cross the road because they saw the bike coming. He has admitted that, there was no zebra crossing at the spot of accident. He has also admitted that, the accused made every possible attempt to avoid the accident and in the process even the accused got injured and he is not aware who shifted the accused to the hospital. 
14. C.W.4 examined as P.W.2 is the eye witness and mahazar witness of this case. He deposed that,
on 14.10.2018 at 12.30 to 1.00 a.m. he, C.W.1 to 3 and 5 CC No.2304/2019 after having food at Koramangala they proceeded towards Trinity in a cab and opposite to Trinity there is one wine shop and there they get down from the cab and they were trying to cross the road and C.W.2 was crossing the road and remaining 4 of them were standing on the divider meanwhile one two wheeler bearing No.TN-58-P- 6924 came in rash and negligent manner and hit to C.W.2, as a result C.W.2 sustained injuries on is head, leg and hand and he was unconscious and shifted to Columbia Asia hospital. On the same day at 9.00 to 10.00 a.m police conducted spot mahazar/Ex.P.1 in his and C.W.1's presence and obtained his signature on it. Further he deposed that, accident has occurred due to the fault of the rider of the offending vehicle. 
15. In his cross examination he has admitted that, they saw the bike from a distance of 8-10 feet and he has also admitted that himself and C.W.2, 3 and 5 did not cross the road because they saw the bike coming. He has admitted that, there was no zebra crossing at the spot of accident. He has also admitted that, the accused made every possible attempt to avoid the accident and in CC No.2304/2019 the process even the accused got injured and he is not aware who shifted the accused to the hospital. 
16. C.W.7 examined as P.W.4 is the IMV Inspector, he deposed about the inspection conducted by him to the offending vehicle bearing No.TN-57-P-6924 and he has given report as per Ex.P.10.
H S Rlay Out Tr Ps vs Maria Robhinath on 24 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/95040995/
4 Further he opined that accident has not occurred due to mechanical defect. He has not been cross examined by the counsel for the accused. 
17. C.W.5 examined as P.W.5 is the eye witness and mahazar witness. He deposed that on 14.10.2018 after having dinner himself, P.W.1, 2, C.W.1 and 2 proceeded in a cab and they get down from the cab near one apartment at Ibbaluru and from the middle of the road they were trying to cross the road at that time his friend Tushar was firstly crossing the road meanwhile one bike bearing No.TN-58-P-6924 came at high speed without headlamp and hit to Tushar , as a result Tushar fell down on road and sustained injuries on his head and face and CC No.2304/2019 shifted to Columbia Asia hospital. On the next day at 9.00 a.m. police conducted spot mahazar/Ex.P.1 in their presence and obtained their signature on it. Further he deposed that, accident has occurred due to the fault of the rider of the offending vehicle. In the accident injured has sustained permanent disability. 
18. In his cross examination he has admitted that, the injured C.W.2 crossed the road without observing the two wheeler. He has admitted that, there was no street lamp at the time of accident. 
He has admitted that, there are plants on the divider and the said road is a heavy traffic road.
19. C.W.10 examined as P.W.3 is the Investigating Officer and he has deposed about the investigation conducted by him. He has admitted that, there is no zebra crossing at the spot of accident. He has admitted that, he has not investigated about the speed of the offending vehicle. He has admitted that, even the accused sustained injuries in the accident. Ex. D.1 to D.6 CC No.2304/2019 photographs have been marked by confronting them to the witness which shows the accused has sustained injuries in the accident and also shows the bad state of the road in which the accident occurred. 
20. With the above evidence, this court has to ascertain whether the prosecution has proved the guilt of the accused beyond all reasonable doubts. In order to prove offence U/Sec.279 of IPC the prosecution has to prove;
(i) Rash and negligent driving on public way (ii) The act must be such as to endanger human life or likely to cause hurt or injury to any person. 
21. To prove an offence U/sec.338 of IPC the prosecution has to prove that some grievous hurt was caused to a person, that such hurt was caused by rash or negligent act of the accused and the act was such that it caused endangerment to human life or public safety of others. 
CC No.2304/2019 22. After marshalling all the oral and documentary evidence it is crystal clear that, in this case the involvement of the offending vehicle bearing registration No.TN-58-P-6924 is not disputed, there is no dispute regarding the accused driving the offending vehicle on the date of the accident. There is no dispute about the injuries sustained by C.W.2. As per wound certificate/Ex.P.9 C.W.2 has H S Rlay Out Tr Ps vs Maria Robhinath on 24 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/95040995/
5 sustained grievous injuries. Hence, there is no dispute that the injuries were sustained by the C.W.2 as a result of accident. There is no dispute regarding IMV report as per Ex.P.10, which states that there is no mechanical defects in the offending vehicle. Hence, the accident did not occur due to any mechanical defects of the vehicles involved in the accident. Since, the injuries of C.W.2 is not disputed, the Court only needs to consider if the accused was driving the offending vehicle in a rash and negligent manner and due to which the accident occurred. 
23. In order to prove that the accused was driving the offending vehicle in a rash or negligent manner the prosecution has examined P.W.1, 2 and 5. All of them in CC No.2304/2019 their cross examination have admitted that, they saw the offending vehicle from a distance of 8-10 feet and they did not cross the road since the bike was coming. They have also admitted that, the accused made every possible attempt to avoid the accident and in that process he also got injured. They have admitted that, there was no zebra crossing in the spot of accident. They have also admitted that,
there was no street light at the spot of the accident. These admissions made by the eye witnesses clearly prove that the injured i.e., C.W.2 has crossed the road negligently without observing the vehicles plying on the road. C.W.2 could not be secured by the prosecution in spite of repeated issuance of summons, warrant and proclamation and he was dropped. The evidence of C.W.2 would have been the best evidence but he could not be secured by the prosecution. Apart from this the prosecution is also relying on the mahazar/Ex.P.1 and rough sketch/Ex.P.5. Mahazar/Ex.P.1 is supported by P.W.1, 2 and 5. In the cross examination all the witnesses have deposed about signing the mahazar at the spot of the accident. Even the accused has not denied the spot of accident because it is the defence of the CC No.2304/2019 accused that he has tried his best to avoid the accident and he has sustained injuries. Even rough sketch/Ex.P.5 is not denied by the accused. But Ex.P.1 and 5 by themselves do not prove the rash and negligent driving of the accused. Further,
prosecution is relying on the wound certificate of C.W.2 to prove the offence U/Sec.338 of IPC. 
There is no dispute regarding the injuries sustained by C.W.2. But merely because grievous injuries are sustained by C.W.2 it cannot be said that the injuries occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the accused. The prosecution is relying on the IMV report as per Ex.P.10 which reveals the damages that occurred to the offending vehicle. Even Ex.P.10 by itself cannot prove rash and negligent driving of the accused. Further the prosecution has examined P.W.7 who has issued Ex.P.10. Since, there is no dispute regarding the damages that occurred to the offending vehicle, the accused has not cross examined P.W.7. But nothing is elicited from his chief examination to prove the rashness or negligence of the accused. Further, prosecution has also examined the I.O., In his cross examination he has admitted that, the road in which the CC No.2304/2019 accident took place was not in a proper condition. He has also admitted that, there is no zebra crossing at the spot of the accident. Hence, even from his evidence it is proved that there is contributory negligence on the part of C.W.2 since he has crossed the road negligently in a place where there was no zebra crossing and without observing the on coming vehicles. 
24. All the eye witnesses have deposed that, the accused has driven his vehicle at a speed of 80 k.m.
per hour. Merely because a vehicle was being driven at a high speed does not mean that the driver was driving rashly or negligently. The Hon'ble Supreme Court in State of Karnataka V/s Sathish reported in 1998 SCC (Cri) 1508 has stated that, driving at a high speed by itself does not imply negligence or rashness. Negligence or rashness would have to be established as a fact. There is only a H S Rlay Out Tr Ps vs Maria Robhinath on 24 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/95040995/
6 bare statement made by P.W.1, 2 and 5 that the offending vehicle was driven at a high speed and rash manner. No attempt has been made to establish that there was rashness on the part of the accused. The expression high speed could range from 30 k.m. per hour CC No.2304/2019 to 100 k.m. per hour. All the 3 eye witnesses state accused was riding at 80 k.m. per hour. But they are not experts to state the speed moreover the speed limit in the particular road is also not on record. 
Therefore in absence of material fact merely because P.W.1, 2 and 5 have alleged that accused was driving at a high speed it cannot be said that the accused is guilty of rash or negligent act. 
25. Reference may be taken from the decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in the case titled "Mohammed Aynuddin @ Miyan vs. State of Andhra Pradesh, reported in (200) 07 SCC 72,
wherein the Hon'ble Apex Court discussed in detail the constituents of a "rash or negligent act" and observed:
"A rash act is primarily an over hasty act. It is opposed to a deliberate act. Still a rash act can be a deliberate act in the sense that it was done without due care and caution. 
Culpable rashness lies in running the risk of CC No.2304/2019 doing an act with recklessness and with indifference as to the consequences. Criminal negligence is the failure to exercise duty with reasonable and proper care and precaution guarding against injury to the public generally or to any individual in particular. It is the imperative duty of the driver of a vehicle to adopt such reasonable and proper care and precaution." Further it is held that it is wrong to presume rashness or negligence on part of the driver for any motor accident. 
26. Therefore, indifference to the consequences of one's act or absence of reasonable care and precaution is the most important ingredient constituting rashness or negligence. It should be noted that intention of the person acting rash or negligent act is immaterial and what is important is that he has not taken due care or has done the said act with indifference to the consequences. Further, it should be noted that there CC No.2304/2019 should be direct nexus between the act or rashness or negligence and hurt/grievous hurt/death, as the case may be, suffered by the victim. In this case P.W.1, 2 and 5 have clearly deposed that the accused did everything possible to avoid the accident. 
This itself shows that the accused was not rash or negligent in driving. Hence, from the evidence of the witnesses examined this Court cannot come to the conclusion that the accident occurred due to the rash or negligent driving of the accused. 
27. It is the burden of the prosecution to prove the guilt of the accused. The evidence placed on record do not rise up to the expectation to prove beyond reasonable doubt in so far as the involvement of accused in the incident is concerned. Therefore, the prosecution version that on the account of rash and negligent driving by the accused, accident has occurred cannot be held to be proved. Since, the accident did not occur due to the negligence or rashness of the accused the liability U/Sec.134(A & B) of IMV Act cannot be imposed on the accused. Moreover, all the witnesses including the I.O. admit that the accused was also involved in the accident CC No.2304/2019 and he was admitted to the hospital. Hence, the accused cannot be expected to comply with Sec.134 ( A & B)
R/w Sec.187 of IMV Act. 
H S Rlay Out Tr Ps vs Maria Robhinath on 24 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/95040995/
7 28. By ascertaining all these oral and documentary evidence it is clear that, there is no substantive,
cogent and corroborative evidence to prove the guilt of the accused. Hence, mere evidence of official witnesses are insufficient to prove the guilt of accused. Therefore, by considering the overall facts and circumstances of this case, this court is of the considered view that the prosecution has failed to prove the guilt of the accused beyond all reasonable doubt. Hence, point Nos.1 to 3 are answered in the negative. 
29. However, the allegation against accused that he is the owner of offending vehicle and he did not possess vehicle insurance on the date of the incident. As there is nothing on record to show that he did possess valid insurance on the date of the offence. Hence, point 4 is answered in the affirmative. 
CC No.2304/2019 30. Point No.5: In view of the findings on point Nos.1 to 4, this court proceeds to pass the following;
 ORDER  Acting under Sec.255(1) of Cr.P.C. accused is hereby acquitted for accusation of commission of the offence punishable U/Sec.279 and 338 of IPC & Sec.134(A & B) R/w Sec.187 of IMV Act.
Acting U/Sec.255(2) of Criminal Procedure code, the accused is hereby convicted of the offences punishable U/Sec.Sec.146 R/w 196 of IMV Act. 
Accused is sentenced to pay fine of Rs.1,000/- (Rupees one thousand only) in default shall undergo simple imprisonment for a period one month for the offence punishable U/Sec.146 R/w 196 of IMV Act. 
 CC No.2304/2019  His bail bond and surety  bond stands cancelled after the  lapse of appeal period. 
(Dictated to the stenographer directly on computer, typed by her, corrected and then pronounced by me in open court on this the 24th day of July, 2024) (Akhila H.K.) JMFC (Traffic Court-VI),
Bengaluru.
